panel.binary.confusions_current_help: Counts at each model’s current threshold. TN: true negative · FP: false positive · FN: false negative · TP: true positive.

panel.binary.hero: Interactive panel to analyze a binary classifier in terms of the positive class, score direction, and operating threshold defined in the configuration.
panel.binary.targets_note: Each row shows which threshold to use to enforce a FAR or FRR constraint and what error remains on the other axis.
panel.binary.far_at_frr_note: Useful when you want to limit rejection of the negative class and see how much of the positive class is lost.
panel.binary.frr_at_far_note: Useful when you want to limit erroneous acceptance of the positive class and see how much rejection appears.
panel.binary.references_note: Standard points to compare the model without enforcing a specific constraint.
panel.binary.worst_note: Misclassified samples at threshold {thr}, ranked by distance to the threshold.
panel.binary.cmp_note: EER and operating FAR/FRR at the configured threshold. Lower values are better.
panel.binary.section.curves.title: Main curves
panel.binary.section.curves.sub: ROC relates true-positive rate to false-positive rate and DET relates false rejection to false acceptance across every score threshold. Curves closer to the favourable corners indicate stronger separation; overlap with the chance region, flat sections or abrupt steps suggest weak ranking, tied scores or limited samples. Compare the same operating region and class definition across models.
panel.binary.section.threshold.title: Threshold decision
panel.binary.section.threshold.sub: FAR and FRR are measured across the score threshold; the vertical line is the configured decision and horizontal lines are the target error rates. Raising the threshold normally trades one error for the other according to score direction. A stable crossing near low rates is favourable, while sharp changes or failure to reach a target indicate an unstable or infeasible operating region.
panel.binary.section.diag.title: Score distributions
panel.binary.section.diag.sub: Class overlap in model scores · Per-model density scales
panel.binary.section.calib.title: Calibration
panel.binary.section.calib.sub: Reliability diagrams and score distribution per bin
panel.multiclass.hero: Global performance, per-class performance, probability calibration and accept/reject behavior — recomputed live with the active filters.
panel.multiclass.chart.confusion.title: Confusion matrix (row %)
panel.multiclass.chart.confusion.sub: Rows are true classes and columns are predicted classes, normalized to 100% within each row. A strong diagonal means stable class recall; large off-diagonal cells identify systematic substitutions. Read every percentage with its class support because rare classes can vary sharply after filtering.
panel.multiclass.chart.perclass.title: Per-class metrics
panel.multiclass.chart.perclass.sub: The table reports support and one-vs-rest Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC for every class. High and similar values indicate balanced behaviour; low recall means missed class instances, low precision means excess assignments, and a large spread between classes reveals uneven performance that a macro average can hide.
panel.multiclass.chart.roc.title: ROC one-vs-rest
panel.multiclass.chart.roc.sub: For each class, the one-vs-rest ROC curve plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate over all thresholds. Curves near the upper-left corner and AUC near 1 indicate strong ranking; the diagonal is chance-like behaviour. Crossings, flat sections or a weak class curve can reveal tied scores, limited support or poor class separation.
panel.multiclass.chart.pr.title: Precision-Recall one-vs-rest
panel.multiclass.chart.pr.sub: Each one-vs-rest curve plots Precision against Recall while the class threshold changes. Curves that retain high precision at high recall are favourable; a steep drop means additional coverage introduces many false positives. PR is prevalence-sensitive, so compare classes together with support and avoid treating small rare-class changes as stable.
panel.multiclass.chart.calib.title: Calibration
panel.multiclass.chart.calib.sub: Predictions are grouped by confidence; each point compares mean confidence with observed accuracy and the bars show bin frequency. Agreement with the diagonal indicates calibration, points below it overconfidence and points above it underconfidence. Sparse extreme bins or an irregular saw-tooth pattern may be sampling noise rather than a reliable correction signal.
panel.multiclass.chart.coverage.title: Accept / reject vs confidence
panel.multiclass.chart.coverage.sub: Coverage is the accepted fraction, accepted accuracy is correctness among retained samples, and rejection is the excluded fraction as minimum confidence increases. Higher thresholds should usually reduce coverage and improve accepted accuracy; plateaus indicate little practical gain, while abrupt jumps suggest clustered scores. The configured and maximum-F1 recommendations are guides, not universal costs.
panel.multiclass.errpairs_help: This table ranks true-to-predicted class pairs within the active selection. Counts identify frequent failure routes and % total gives their overall impact; a concentrated pair suggests a systematic boundary problem, while many small pairs indicate diffuse confusion. Sorting or filtering changes the evidence slice, not the class definitions.
panel.multiclass.no_confusions: No confusions in the current selection
panel.multiclass.worst_note: Misclassified samples ranked by confidence (high-confidence errors first).
panel.age.hero: Multi-model age-estimation evaluation · MAE / Acc@N (NIST) · Compliance operating points (B-ACC, FAR, FRR) · Binary classification curves · FPR heatmap by age and challenge
panel.age.summary_desc: Global accuracy over the selected images. MAE in years; Acc@Ny = predictions with |error| ≤ N years; SD = error dispersion. Active filters recompute every value.
panel.age.compliance_desc: For each age threshold and FAR target, the minimum decision threshold Y* is found such that P(pred ≥ Y* | gt < AGE_TH) ≤ target. At that Y*, B-ACC, Accuracy and FRR are measured. A high B-ACC indicates a good balance between protecting minors and admitting adults.
panel.age.challenge_desc: MAE and dispersion over images with real age between {min_age} and T−1 for each Challenge-T. This subgroup concentrates the hardest cases to classify. Active filters.
panel.age.band_desc: MAE per 5-year band over the selected images. Identifies where the model is least accurate. Active filters.
panel.age.heatmap_title: FPR Heatmap by Age and Challenge
panel.age.heatmap_desc: Each cell is P(predicted age ≥ challenge | actual age = row age), with counts available as failures/total. Values near 0% mean few underage samples cross that challenge; high or isolated red cells identify risky ages, while a stable rising band near the boundary is expected. Sparse rows can fluctuate strongly, and empty cells are outside the defined underage comparison.
panel.age.dist_desc: The filled curves are Gaussian kernel-density estimates of actual and predicted ages. Their area is normalized to one, so compare distribution shape rather than raw sample count. Displaced peaks suggest systematic age shift; gaps or different tails indicate sampling or model-behaviour differences. Hover to inspect age, density, sample count and bandwidth.
panel.age.sweep_desc: For each legal or study age threshold, the decision rule predicted age ≥ Y is swept across Y and reports Accuracy, FAR, FRR and balanced accuracy. Increasing Y usually lowers false acceptance but raises false rejection. High, stable balanced accuracy near the natural threshold is favourable; sharp crossings or unattainable FAR targets expose an unstable operating choice.
panel.age.visual_desc: These linked views inspect individual predictions and signed error in years. Use them after the aggregate tables to distinguish random dispersion, age-dependent bias and isolated cases; colour is a slice aid and never changes the underlying estimates.
panel.age.scatter_desc: Each point compares predicted and actual age in years; the diagonal is exact agreement. A narrow, stable cloud around the line indicates low error, points above it overestimate and points below it underestimate. Curvature, widening spread or colour clusters suggest age-dependent bias, heteroscedasticity or a subgroup that needs separate review.
panel.age.variation_desc: Residual is predicted minus actual age in years. Values near 0 indicate little signed error, sustained positive or negative bands indicate over- or underestimation, and increasing spread with age indicates variable precision. Abrupt isolated residuals are worst-case candidates rather than evidence of a general trend.
panel.age.pairwise_desc: For aligned images, the filled KDE estimates the distribution of the absolute difference between both models’ absolute age errors. Density near 0 means similar per-image performance; a long right tail reveals cases where their errors diverge. This magnitude is not directional, so inspect paired rows before deciding which model is better.
panel.age.range_desc: MAE and RMSE summarize absolute and squared error in five-year actual-age bands, in years; Bias is mean predicted minus actual age. Low, stable MAE/RMSE and Bias near 0 are favourable. Rising error, RMSE far above MAE or sustained signed Bias identifies tail failures, variable precision or systematic age-range drift.
panel.age.worst_note: Cases ranked by absolute age error (computed on the full data).
panel.ocr.hero: OCR panel to evaluate transcriptions and structured per-field extraction. Its three primary metrics are character error rate, complete-word Recall and strict whole-document Accuracy.
panel.ocr.main_desc: These cards are recomputed dynamically based on the active filters.
panel.ocr.segment_desc: Each row aggregates unique documents and evaluated fields for the active grouping variable, then reports normalized CER, word Recall and strict document Accuracy. Accuracy includes exact/total documents in parentheses; one incorrect field makes its document incorrect.
panel.ocr.field_desc: Each row isolates one structured field and reports support, normalized CER, word Recall and the Missing rate. Stable low error across fields suggests consistent extraction; high Missing points to absent output, while high CER with low Missing means text was produced but transcribed incorrectly. Critical identifiers should be reviewed even with small support.
panel.ocr.heatmap_desc: Cells cross the selected segment with each field and always display the selected percentage with support in parentheses: value (n/total). Low CER/Missing and high Recall are favourable; isolated extremes with low support require evidence review rather than ranking.
panel.ocr.errtypes_desc: The pie shows the share of substitutions, insertions, deletions and completely missing fields in the active selection. Slice area compares each cause with the total error burden; substitution dominance suggests character discrimination, deletion/missing suggests cropping or detection loss, and insertion may indicate background being read as text.
panel.ocr.confusions_desc: Bars rank recurring ground-truth-to-predicted character pairs and split them by the active segment. High repeated counts expose systematic confusions such as 0/O; isolated pairs may follow rare content. Interpret frequency with field semantics because one identifier or checksum error can matter more than several descriptive-text errors.
panel.ocr.worst_desc: Top K among fields with errors only. Correctly predicted samples are excluded and the characters causing the failure are highlighted in red.
panel.ocr.normimpact_desc: The left lane links raw and normalized CER (Character) for each field. The right lane decomposes field records into unchanged, normalized but still non-exact, and exact matches recovered. Separation between markers reveals metric dependence on preprocessing; a dominant recovered share indicates useful equivalence handling, while no separation with many modified records means formatting changed without improving recognition.
panel.ocr.normpanel_desc: Metrics are computed over normalized GT and normalized prediction. The table shows generic examples of each rule and indicates whether that rule is currently active in the computation.
panel.ocr.no_cases: No OCR cases with errors in the current selection.
panel.ocr.other_model_note: Interactive OCR dashboard generated for the first model. This model is available in the consolidated Excel report.
panel.regression.hero: Regression panel: global error, bias, dispersion, calibration, per-segment breakdown and worst cases — recomputed live with the active filters.
panel.regression.segment_note: Per-segment breakdown over the primary filter variable (computed on the full data).
panel.regression.worst_note: Top cases ranked by absolute error (computed on the full data).
panel.regression.chart.pred.title: Prediction vs actual
panel.regression.chart.pred.sub: Each point compares prediction with the actual target in the target’s native unit; the y=x line is exact agreement. A tight stable cloud indicates low error, vertical displacement indicates bias, widening spread indicates heteroscedasticity, and isolated distant points are anomalous cases. Curvature suggests the model response is miscalibrated across the range.
panel.regression.chart.resid.title: Residuals vs prediction
panel.regression.chart.resid.sub: Residual is prediction minus actual value in the target’s native unit and is plotted against prediction. A narrow random band around 0 is favourable; a sustained positive or negative band indicates bias, a funnel indicates changing variance, and waves or curvature indicate missing non-linearity. Abrupt extremes are tail errors to audit.
panel.regression.chart.calib.title: Interval calibration
panel.regression.chart.calib.sub: Actual targets are grouped into equal-width bins and each point compares mean actual with mean predicted value in the native unit. Agreement with the diagonal indicates interval calibration; systematic separation indicates under- or overprediction. Oscillation or isolated bins can reflect local bias or weak bin support.
panel.regression.chart.dist.title: Residual KDE
panel.regression.chart.dist.sub: The filled Gaussian kernel-density estimate shows prediction-minus-actual residuals in the target’s native unit. A compact curve centred on 0 indicates low unbiased error; a displaced peak indicates signed bias, broad tails indicate variable precision, and asymmetry or multiple modes can reveal subgroups or unusual failure mechanisms.
panel.regression.chart.qq.title: Residual QQ plot
panel.regression.chart.qq.sub: Ordered residual quantiles are compared with theoretical normal quantiles. Points close to the reference line indicate approximately normal residual shape; bowed tails indicate heavy or light tails, asymmetric departures indicate skew, and isolated endpoints reveal extreme errors. Normality is diagnostic, not a requirement for prediction quality.
panel.regression.chart.cum.title: Cumulative absolute-error curve
panel.regression.chart.cum.sub: For every absolute-error limit in the target’s native unit, the curve reports the fraction of samples at or below that limit. A rapid rise toward 100% is favourable; a slow rise or long plateau exposes tail failures. Read application tolerances directly from the x-axis rather than selecting a threshold after seeing the result.

panel.object_detection.hero: A visual evaluation workspace for ranking quality, operating-point errors and auditable image-level debugging.
panel.segmentation.hero: A scientific workspace for overlap, boundaries, calibration and image-level segmentation evidence.
panel.object_detection.workbench_help: Filters and operating controls recalculate threshold-dependent metrics and cases; they never alter AP, AP@75 or the 101-point PR curves.
panel.object_detection.overview_help: Threshold-free ranking quality is separated from the configurable operating point so a confidence change cannot be mistaken for a new AP result.
panel.object_detection.classes_help: Search, order and inspect the same class metrics used in global averages. Support remains visible so rare classes are not ranked as if they were equally stable.
panel.object_detection.dataset_help: These descriptive plots use canonical boxes to expose image, class, position, scale and shape coverage. They diagnose the evaluation dataset and never change AP or matching.
panel.object_detection.errors_help: Every active prediction receives one exclusive error category and unmatched references create independent missed-ground-truth events. Counts change with confidence and Matching IoU.
panel.object_detection.cases_help: Embedded source images retain responsive GT, prediction, TP, FP and FN overlays. Filters and ordering select evidence for review; they do not recompute AP.
panel.object_detection.quality_help: Canonical conversions, warnings, image dimensions and project-defined size ranges remain visible here and traceable in the Excel evidence package.
panel.object_detection.chart_tools_hint: Pan, zoom, select and export from the always-visible chart toolbar.
panel.object_detection.threshold_free_he: AP uses 101 recall levels and all predictions ranked by descending confidence. Matching restarts independently for each class and IoU threshold.
panel.object_detection.operating_help: Confidence and Matching IoU affect TP, FP, FN, Precision, Recall, F1, matched IoU, error categories and cases only.
panel.object_detection.severity_help: Missed 6 · combined 5 · classification 4 · localization 3 · duplicate 2 · background 1 · TP 0.
panel.object_detection.protocol_warning: COCO-style metric, not the full COCO protocol.
panel.object_detection.confusion_help: Rows are ground-truth classes and columns are predictions, with background and missed states. A strong diagonal is favourable; large off-diagonal cells reveal systematic class substitutions, while background/missed concentration distinguishes false alarms from absent detections. Read percentages with row support.
panel.object_detection.chart.sweep.title: Precision · Recall · F1
panel.object_detection.chart.sweep.help: The curves recalculate Precision, Recall and F1 from detections at or above each confidence threshold, using the active Matching IoU. Low thresholds usually increase Recall and false positives; high thresholds usually increase Precision and misses. A broad F1 plateau is stable, while narrow peaks or abrupt steps indicate score clustering or limited support.
panel.object_detection.chart.pr.title: Precision–Recall by class
panel.object_detection.chart.pr.help: The selected class uses score-ranked, one-to-one matches at IoU 0.50 and 101 interpolated recall levels. Curves retaining high Precision at high Recall and larger AP are favourable. A steep drop indicates high-scoring false positives; flat or stepped segments may reflect few references or tied scores.
panel.object_detection.chart.class_map.h: Each cell prints the selected class metric for one model, from 0 to 1. High AP/F1/IoU is favourable; consistently weak columns identify difficult classes and isolated weak cells identify a model-specific failure. Compare support before interpreting large differences in rare classes.
panel.object_detection.chart.image_dimen: Each point is an image width × height in pixels and bubble area reflects objects per image. Broad coverage indicates varied canvases; tight clusters mean limited resolution/aspect-ratio evidence. Isolated sizes or unusually dense bubbles can expose preprocessing, batching or annotation anomalies.
panel.object_detection.chart.class_frequ: Bars count ground-truth or predicted boxes for each class under the active geometry scope. Similar counts support balanced evaluation; very low classes yield unstable AP and high prediction-to-reference excess can indicate false positives or duplicates. Abrupt imbalance should guide sampling and error review.
panel.object_detection.chart.center_dens: Normalized box centres (x,y from 0 to 1; top-left origin) are accumulated as density. Even coverage means positions are broadly represented; hot central or edge regions reveal spatial priors. Empty zones are untested geometry, while isolated points may be rare scenes or coordinate errors.
panel.object_detection.chart.box_size.he: Normalized box width and height (0–1 of the image) form a scale/shape density map. Compact clusters indicate a narrow object-size regime; broad coverage tests more geometry. Edge concentrations, impossible-looking shapes or isolated extremes can indicate clipping, annotation or conversion problems.
panel.object_detection.chart.box_atlas.h: Up to 300 normalized boxes are translated to the same centre without changing width or height. Similar outlines reveal dominant shapes; diverse footprints show scale/aspect coverage. Very large, thin or isolated boxes should be checked against images because the atlas describes geometry, not correctness.
panel.object_detection.chart.errors.help: Counts separate missed ground truth, combined, classification, localization, duplicate and background errors at the active thresholds. Low, stable counts are favourable. Misses suggest coverage, classification suggests label boundaries, localization suggests box placement, and background/duplicates suggest excess detections.
panel.object_detection.chart.iou.title: TP IoU distribution
panel.object_detection.chart.iou.help: IoU from 0 to 1 is shown only for true-positive matches at the current confidence and Matching IoU. Mass near 1 indicates tight boxes; concentration near the threshold indicates fragile localization. A broad or multimodal distribution suggests class, size or scene-dependent precision; an empty plot means no qualifying matches.
panel.object_detection.chart.fpfn.title: FP and FN by class
panel.object_detection.chart.fpfn.help: Bars count false-positive predictions and missed ground-truth instances per class at the active operating point. Low balanced counts are favourable; FP dominance suggests permissive confidence or class confusion, while FN dominance suggests poor coverage or an overly strict threshold. Read counts with class support before comparing classes.

eye.chart.help.aggregates: This panel reflects available summaries at trial, session and participant level while preserving each metric's declared unit. Stable, similar values within the same metric suggest reproducible behaviour across groups; wide variation or isolated extremes identify a context that may be driving the overall result. High and low values are not universally good or bad—the interpretation depends on the metric and unit. Use the panel to locate heterogeneity for audit, not to rank unlike measurements or participants.
eye.chart.help.angular: This panel reflects the distribution of angular disagreement between the predicted and reference gaze vectors for each model, measured in degrees. Low values concentrated near 0° indicate accurate and consistent direction estimates; a high median suggests systematic model error, while a long upper tail identifies occasional severe failures. In practice, the centre and spread distinguish persistent calibration bias from isolated problematic samples.
eye.chart.help.compliance: This panel reflects the percentage of comparable samples whose angular error remains within each configured limit in degrees. High attainment at strict thresholds indicates precise predictions; low attainment that improves only when the limit is relaxed means the model is broadly directional but insufficiently accurate. Comparing the threshold steps shows which tolerance is realistic for the intended experimental use.
eye.chart.help.coverage: This panel reflects the spatial coverage of valid gaze samples in a 20 × 20 grid over normalized coordinates. High cell counts indicate regions visited repeatedly or for longer periods; low counts indicate brief passage, and empty cells mean no recorded gaze there—not a visual deficit. A stable concentration may be consistent with a focused task, while an even distribution indicates broader exploration. Practically, it checks whether the trial sampled the expected parts of the scene.
eye.chart.help.gaze2d: This panel reflects where reference and predicted gaze fall on the same canonical screen plane, in pixels; each connecting segment is the error for one sample. Overlapping points and short, stable segments indicate accurate screen localization. A consistent horizontal or vertical offset suggests calibration bias, whereas changing directions and long segments reveal variable error or local tracking failures. The spatial pattern helps identify whether errors are global or concentrated in particular screen regions.
eye.chart.help.gaze3d: This panel reflects the signed yaw and pitch residuals of the selected model in degrees. A compact, stable cloud around (0°, 0°) indicates no relevant directional bias; displacement to one side reveals systematic horizontal or vertical overestimation. A broad cloud means inconsistent prediction, and isolated distant points may correspond to unusual poses, tracking loss or model failure. The quadrant pattern indicates which directional correction would be required.
eye.chart.help.landmarks: This panel reflects the normalized mean error (NME) for each periocular landmark: Euclidean localization error divided by the configured anatomical or image reference, so the value is unitless. Low and similar values across landmarks indicate stable ocular geometry. A high value confined to one landmark suggests local occlusion or a difficult structure; high values across all landmarks may indicate scale, crop or alignment failure. The comparison identifies which anatomical points require model or annotation review.
eye.chart.help.scene_dwell: This panel reflects interaction timing for each configured AOI: gaze-sample dwell and supplied-fixation dwell are measured in seconds, and first response is the delay from trial onset to the first qualifying fixation. High dwell indicates longer recorded viewing within the object region; low dwell suggests a brief pass, while a short first-response time means early entry. N/A means no supplied fixation satisfied the AOI rule. The comparison helps distinguish immediate inspection from late or transient viewing without inferring attention by itself.
eye.chart.help.scene_heatmap: This panel reflects where the participant looked in the first-person scene: normalized scene Gaze X/Y (0–1) produces the heat intensity, while the line preserves scanpath order. A stable hot zone indicates repeated or sustained viewing of the same scene region; abrupt jumps between zones indicate gaze transitions. Diffuse heat or isolated points may represent broad exploration, movement or imprecise tracking. The overlay helps relate the viewing sequence to the table, hand and object shown in the replay.
eye.chart.help.segmentation: This panel reflects agreement between predicted and reference pupil/iris masks through IoU, Dice and boundary IoU on a 0–1 scale. Values stable near 1 indicate strong overlap and a correctly delimited contour; low values indicate missing or excess segmented area. High Dice with low boundary IoU means the region size is broadly correct but its edge is inaccurate. The metric combination separates gross mask failure from a contour-specific problem.
eye.chart.help.slices: This panel reflects how mean model error changes within each eligible experimental slice relative to the overall mean, expressed as a percentage. Values stable around 0% indicate comparable performance across that condition; positive values indicate higher error and negative values lower error. Large changes may reveal sensitivity to lighting, scenario or participant context, but must be read with group size, confidence interval and effect size. Practically, it identifies conditions that require targeted robustness review.
eye.chart.help.spatial: This panel reflects how gaze explored the normalized field (X/Y from 0 to 1) by combining sample density, supplied fixations and the time-ordered scanpath. A compact, stable cluster suggests prolonged viewing of one region; separated clusters connected by rapid transitions indicate shifts between targets. A broad or fragmented trace may represent active exploration, but when accompanied by sparse density it can also signal noisy tracking. The view is useful for reconstructing the viewing strategy without treating density as proof of attention.
eye.chart.help.stability: This panel reflects eye-movement dynamics through normalized gaze displacement per second and rolling RMS jitter. Low, stable velocity suggests fixation or no relevant displacement; velocity peaks indicate saccades or rapid gaze shifts. Low jitter means local signal stability, whereas high or changing jitter may indicate tremor, noise, reduced precision, micro-instability, tracking loss or a fast movement transition.
eye.chart.help.timeline: This panel reflects the temporal evolution of normalized gaze position (Gaze X/Y, 0–1), tracking confidence (0–1) and pupil diameter in millimetres. Stable Gaze X/Y suggests a maintained fixation, whereas abrupt coordinate changes indicate gaze displacement. Low confidence may reflect poor detection quality, occlusion, blinking or unstable tracking. A stable pupil diameter indicates no relevant physiological change; abrupt or sustained contraction/dilation may be associated with the stimulus, visual effort or a physiological reflex, but also with motion or measurement noise.
eye.common.no_records: No records available for this capability or selection.
eye.controls.scope.help: Participant, session, trial and model context is preserved across evidence and exports.
eye.description.aggregates: Available dimensions are grouped without treating frames as independent participants or inventing missing metadata.
eye.description.cases: Missing predictions rank before large matched errors. Every row retains its sample and target identity.
eye.description.coverage: Spatial coverage uses the configured normalized grid and is not a clinical visual-field measurement.
eye.description.dictionary: Meaning, type, unit and reference frame travel with every canonical field.
eye.description.evaluation: Five decision metrics are recomputed for the active model and sample scope. The eye-specific table exposes asymmetry instead of hiding it in one aggregate.
eye.description.evaluation.regions: Ground-truth and predicted gaze vectors are assigned to Up, Down, Left, Right or Center. Center uses the configured angular band; outside it, the dominant yaw or pitch axis defines the region.
eye.description.evaluation.screen: Paired reference and prediction points use the declared canonical screen coordinate system. Connecting segments reveal both error magnitude and systematic direction.
eye.description.events: No fixation detector is applied implicitly. The table is empty when events were not supplied.
eye.description.evidence: Audit what is available, how each result was built and which source fields support it. Missing capabilities remain visible.
eye.description.evidence_validation: Warnings, unavailable capabilities, units, coordinate systems, synchronization and derivations remain visible and exportable.
eye.description.gaze: Numbers precede each graph; the Plotly toolbar remains available for inspection and export.
eye.description.geometry: Landmark error is normalized by the configured anatomical/image reference; masks use pixel-level diagnostics.
eye.description.interaction: TTFF is unavailable when no supplied fixation reaches the AOI; gaze-sample dwell remains available.
eye.description.provenance: Algorithm version, parameters and source tables make derived evidence reproducible.
eye.description.reconstruction: Inspect the pupil centroid, limbus reference, confidence field and projected gaze vector in instrument coordinates. The view is a technical schematic derived from supplied measurements, never a reconstruction of participant anatomy.
eye.description.recording: Periocular geometry and the first-person scene share participant, session, trial, recording and time. Tracker confidence is kept separate from observed movement variability.
eye.description.robustness: Robustness is a configurable descriptive index. It is not a clinical score.
eye.description.scene: Review scene frames, gaze uncertainty and supplied AOIs on the same recording cursor. Sample dwell and fixation dwell remain distinct.
eye.description.slices: Minimum group size, confidence interval, significance and standardized effect are preserved in the report.
eye.description.temporal: Temporal comparison is only reported when GT and prediction share an explicit event identifier.
eye.description.timeline: The current cursor is marked without altering the underlying recording.
eye.description.validation: Coordinate conversions are explicit. Camera, head and world frames are never mixed automatically.

eye.visual.help.direction: This view reflects how normalized gaze samples are distributed across left, right, up, down and centre. A stable dominant zone indicates a consistent viewing direction; balanced counts indicate broader exploration, and rapid changes may be eye movement or noise. It summarizes directional behaviour in the recording and is not a clinical visual-field result.
eye.visual.help.scene_replay: This view reflects the participant's first-person scene at the shared trial time. Gaze and uncertainty use normalized image coordinates (0–1), the trail preserves temporal order, and AOI/object rectangles identify configured regions. A compact, stable gaze trace supports sustained inspection; abrupt jumps show transitions, while diffuse uncertainty or missing overlays reduce confidence in precise localization. Reading the sequence alongside the cursor connects the empty table, object placement, approach and withdrawal phases.

panel.binary.logit_bias_help: Additive decision bias b = −logit(t) = ln((1 − t) / t). On a probability-score scale, p ≥ t is equivalent to logit(p) + b ≥ 0 (reverse the inequality for lower-positive scores). At t = 0 or 1, the displayed infinity is a limit; outside [0, 1], the bias is unavailable. This is an operating-point transformation, not a fitted model parameter.

panel.binary.curves.detHelp: DET uses normal-deviate (probit) axes. Rates below 0.1% are drawn at the lower boundary; hover reports the actual rate. The upper window expands to include current operating points (up to 99.9%). Curves outside the window are omitted; use autoscale to inspect plotted points.

panel.binary.distributions.kdeHelp: Each class density integrates to one. Gaussian KDE uses Scott's bandwidth, with reflection at 0 and 1 for bounded scores. A class with fewer than two distinct scores uses a density histogram. The vertical line is that model's current threshold. AUC, EER and AP use the selected rows and do not depend on the current threshold. Density axes auto-scale per model so narrow peaks do not flatten the other cards. EER retains the report's threshold-grid estimate.
panel.binary.distributions.calibrationHe: For each class, compare its mean predicted probability with its observed frequency in each bin. The negative class uses 1 − p(positive); these are complementary views, not independent estimates. The lower histogram groups positive-class probabilities by true label; its bars sum to 100% across both classes. Empty bins are omitted. Calibration is unavailable outside [0, 1].
panel.binary.distributions.eceHelp: ECE retains the report definition: 10 equal-width bins. The Bins control changes the diagrams and histograms only, not ECE or Brier.
panel.binary.distributions.combinedKey: Model colour · Positive: solid · Negative: dashed · Histogram: true-class groups (negative hatched)
